brief: Wiremu Tāmihana’s original name was Tarapīpi Te Waharoa. He was the second son of the Ngāti Haua chief, Te Waharoa. He was deeply influenced by missionary teaching. He created a marae near Matamata which became known for its peaceful Christian witness. He earned the title, “kingmaker”, in the creation of the first of the Waikato kings. He tried to mediate during the land wars and negotiated a settlement when they ended. He wrote many letters to colonial authorities advocating a just provision for Māori and Pākehā. He died in 1866.
